questions.question: Which part of the Constitution establishes the formal amendment process?
choices: Article II
Article V
Article I
Article VII

questions.question: What fraction of both houses of Congress is required to propose a constitutional amendment?
choices: Two-thirds
One-half
Three-fourths
Four-fifths

questions.question: What fraction of states must ratify a proposed constitutional amendment?
choices: One-half
Two-thirds
Four-fifths
Three-fourths

questions.question: Which amendment delays changes in congressional pay until after an election for the House of Representatives?
choices: Twentieth
Twenty-Second
Twenty-Seventh
Twenty-Fifth

questions.question: Which amendment includes the Equal Protection Clause applying to states?
choices: Fourteenth
Tenth
Sixteenth
Twenty-First

questions.question: Which amendment prohibits denial of voting rights because of race, color, or previous condition of servitude?
choices: Nineteenth
Fifteenth
Twenty-Fourth
Twenty-Sixth

questions.question: Which amendment prohibits denying the vote to citizens age 18 or older because of age?
choices: Twenty-Second
Twenty-Third
Twenty-Sixth
Twenty-Fifth

questions.question: Why does the amendment process require broad support?
choices: To make constitutional changes identical to ordinary bills
To give the president sole authority to alter the document
To allow one state to replace the entire Constitution
To balance the possibility of change with constitutional stability

questions.question: What is the president's formal role in approving an amendment proposed by Congress?
choices: Presidential signature or veto is not part of that process
The president must sign it before states can consider it
The president alone decides which states may ratify it
A presidential veto requires unanimous state ratification

questions.question: How did the Twelfth Amendment change the Electoral College process?
choices: It replaced electors with a national popular vote
It required separate electoral votes for president and vice president
It gave each state exactly one electoral vote
It transferred all presidential selection to the Supreme Court

questions.question: What is the general purpose of the Twenty-Second Amendment?
choices: To replace the vice presidency with a cabinet council
To give the president an unlimited number of terms
To require annual presidential elections
To limit how many times a person may be elected president

questions.question: What issue does the Twenty-Fifth Amendment address?
choices: Direct election of senators
Congressional income tax authority
Presidential succession, vice-presidential vacancies, and inability
Voting rights in state school-board elections

questions.question: How did the Twenty-First Amendment relate to the Eighteenth Amendment?
choices: It repealed the earlier prohibition amendment
It extended prohibition to additional products
It made prohibition a permanent unamendable rule
It transferred prohibition enforcement to foreign courts

questions.question: What did the Twenty-Fourth Amendment prohibit in federal elections?
choices: The use of secret ballots
Poll taxes as a condition of voting
The election of candidates without party membership
Registration procedures for eligible voters

questions.question: What did the Twenty-Third Amendment provide for the District of Columbia?
choices: Full statehood under the Constitution
Two voting senators and no electors
The power to ratify amendments as a state
Participation in presidential elections through appointed electors

questions.question: A proposal passes both houses of Congress by two-thirds, but only half the states ratify it. What is its status?
choices: It becomes law after presidential approval
It takes effect only in the ratifying states
It has not become a constitutional amendment
It automatically goes to the Supreme Court for adoption

questions.question: Which alternative to congressional proposal is authorized by Article V?
choices: A convention called after applications from two-thirds of state legislatures
A national petition signed by one million voters
A presidential proclamation approved by cabinet members
A unanimous decision of the federal courts of appeals

questions.question: Which distinction between an ordinary federal law and a constitutional amendment is correct?
choices: Ordinary laws require ratification by three-fourths of states
Amendments alter the constitutional framework through a separate process
Ordinary laws cannot be repealed after presidential signature
Amendments require the same simple-majority procedure as bills

questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders these voting-rights amendments by ratification?
choices: Twenty-Sixth → Nineteenth → Fifteenth
Nineteenth → Fifteenth → Twenty-Sixth
Fifteenth → Nineteenth → Twenty-Sixth
Fifteenth → Twenty-Sixth → Nineteenth

questions.question: A student says ratifying the Fifteenth Amendment immediately ended racial voting barriers. Which evidence best challenges this claim?
choices: The amendment's number comes after fourteen
Presidential elections continued after ratification
States retained elected legislatures
Discriminatory practices continued despite the constitutional prohibition
